summary: Implemented an in-app SSH terminal (xterm.js frontend + a Windows ConPTY-backed ssh.exe session via portable-pty), matching the Pi Control design's terminal modal, while keeping the WU016 external-launch fallback chain available as a secondary action. Discovered and fixed a real deadlock in the reader/waiter thread design during development (documented in code and tests). cargo test 164/164 + 1 intentionally-ignored slow regression test proving ConPTY genuinely works in this environment.
completed: platform/pty.rs: PtySessionManager spawns `ssh.exe -tt [-p <port>] <user>@<host>` in a ConPTY via portable-pty, with a reader thread (streams output) and a separate waiter thread (blocks on child exit, then removes the session -- which drops the pty master and is what actually unblocks the reader's read on Windows, since ConPTY only delivers EOF once the console object itself is torn down, not merely once the child exits).
commands/terminal.rs: open_terminal_session / write_terminal_input / resize_terminal_session / close_terminal_session Tauri commands.

features/terminal/TerminalModal.tsx: xterm.js terminal UI matching the design's dark terminal-modal chrome, portaled to document.body to avoid React's tree-based event bubbling reaching a card's onClick.

features/terminal/LazyTerminalModal.tsx: React.lazy() code-splits xterm.js into its own chunk, only fetched when a terminal is opened -- confirmed via build output (~330KB separate chunk, main bundle unaffected).
DeviceCard.tsx / DeviceDetailScreen.tsx: primary Open Terminal action now opens the embedded modal; DeviceDetailScreen keeps a secondary icon button for the WU016 external-launch path.

1 new #[ignore]'d regression test (native_pty_spawns_a_process_and_captures_its_output) proving the ConPTY/portable-pty mechanism genuinely works on this machine; ignored by default since a real console spawn took 30+ seconds in this environment (default suite stays sub-second).
Verified cargo build (clean) and cargo test (164/164, 1 ignored); npm run build and npm run lint (0 errors, 3 pre-existing warnings).

validationCommands.summary: 164/164 passed, 1 intentionally ignored (slow ConPTY regression test, run manually via --ignored).
TypeScript build succeeds; xterm.js confirmed split into its own lazy-loaded chunk.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: In-app terminal modal/panel rendering a live SSH session
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: TerminalModal renders an xterm.js Terminal wired to open_terminal_session/terminal://output/write_terminal_input; PtySessionManager's underlying spawn/read/write/wait mechanism is proven working on this machine via the (manually run) native_pty_spawns_a_process_and_captures_its_output test.

notes: Risk score: 40/100 (medium). Rationale: genuinely new, non-trivial OS-integration surface (raw ConPTY process management with two cooperating background threads per session) -- higher than any other WU in this project's backlog. Mitigated by: the reader/waiter split was arrived at by actually reproducing and fixing a real deadlock during development (not theoretical), a passing regression test proves the core mechanism works on this exact machine, and the command layer itself is a thin, structurally-proven pattern identical to every other SSH-backed command.

Development note for posterity: an early single-thread design (read-to-completion, then wait()) deadlocked for real against a live cmd.exe process -- cmd's write of its output blocked on ConPTY's pipe buffer waiting for a reader, while nothing read until wait() (which needed the child to exit) returned. A second attempt (wait-then-read sequentially) also deadlocked, for the mirror-image reason. The fix -- concurrent reader and waiter threads, plus always taking (even if unused) the pty writer per portable-pty's own documented warning -- is now the production design, not just the test's workaround.

Live click-through verification (actually opening a session, typing, seeing a prompt) was not performed in this sandboxed session -- no input-injection tool is available that doesn't risk a stray click on the real desktop, consistent with the same limitation noted in WU020's checkpoint. Recommend the user try opening a terminal against a real device as a final confirmation; the underlying spawn mechanism, output streaming, and command wiring are all independently verified as described above.

Bundle-size awareness: xterm.js is a substantial dependency (~330KB); lazy-loading via React.lazy() keeps it out of the app's normal startup path entirely, so it has no effect on the ~3-second startup budget or idle resource usage measured earlier in this conversation.
